title.narrative: Output 3.3. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement policies for a just transition towards environmentally sustainable economies and societies

description.narrative: In South Africa the Government (Presidential Climate Commission, PCC) in consultation with social partners and communities across the country, adopted A Framework for a Just Transition in May 2022 for the entire country drawing on “ILO Guidelines for a just transition towards environmentally sustainable economies and societies for all”. The Framework for a Just Transition builds on research, policies, and consultations on the just transition in South Africa, as well as international best practice guidelines. It defines a just transition as a process contributing to the goals of decent work for all, social inclusion, and the eradication of poverty; a transition that puts people at the centre of decision-making, particularly those most impacted by climate and environmental change, people in situations of poverty, women, people with disabilities, and the youth. The Framework for a Just Transition recognizes that women are particularly vulnerable to the effects of climate change and other forms of environmental degradation and that solutions to climate change are documented to be more effective when involving women. South Africa’s Framework for a Just Transition is aligned to Nationally Determined Contributions, environmental goals and development priorities. During the previous biennium the ILO engaged with the PCC where the ILO gave presentations on the ILO’s Just Transition Guidelines, emphasizing the principles of social dialogue and stakeholder consultation, and policy coherence for a Just Transition; And where the ILO engaged in a joint meeting with the ITUC and PCC where the ILO shared and facilitated discussion on Just Transition best practices from around the world. In February 2023 the ILO provided guidance to the PCC on how to consult with Organized Labour on policy initiatives for a Just Transition. This shaped Organized Labour dialogues hosted by the PCC in March 2023 for the implementation of the Framework for a Just Transition.

Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises and their support systems to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative:
The Government of South Africa in close consultation with the Social Partners developed and launched Productivity Measurements in October 2023 to strengthen the capacity of Productivity-South Africa (SA) to expand the scope of its productivity measurements and to examine key policy questions. The Government established a tripartite Technical Advisory Group (TAG) as a vehicle of engagement with the Social Partners to develop the Productivity Measurements. The Capacity building support provided to Productivity-SA in this regard, builds on current practices of quality standards and data comparability and context in South Africa, including Productivity SA’s annual productivity reports. The development of the productivity measures is underpinned by international standards and guidance from the United Nations System of National Accounts (UN SNA) and OECD Manual on Productivity. The intention is to improve the measurements of productivity and its use for policy reform. In October 2023 the Gauteng Automotive Industry Development Centre (AIDC), an agency of the Gauteng Department of Economic Development, launched a training curriculum that incorporates entrepreneurship into the Centre’s technical training. The objective of the curriculum is to prepare youth who choose the entrepreneurship pathway to identify a business idea, prepare business plans and start a business. The curriculum targets mainly youth owned start-ups and small enterprises. From June -2023 to October-2023 a cadre of trainers on the AIDC’s enterprise curriculum was established to roll-out the training of Start Your Business for youth owned start-ups and small enterprises located in selected townships within the Gauteng province. In June 2023, with support from the Governments of Switzerland and Norway, the ILO supported Government in the establishment of a tripartite Technical Advisory Group (TAG) to provide technical oversight for the development of Productivity Measurements in South Africa. The membership of the TAG was comprised of representatives from National Government Departments, and the Social Partners and Government Agencies. In June 2023, the ILO facilitated and coordinated a meeting of a Technical Working Group, a subset of the TAG, to discuss the state and scope of productivity statistics in South Africa, including such data generated by key institutions such as Productivity SA, Statistics South Africa and the South African Reserve Bank. In September 2023 the ILO reviewed the National Accounts and Labour data from Statistics SA and Productivity SA and trained key personnel from Statistics South Africa and Productivity SA on advanced productivity computations.
In June 2023, with the support of the Government of Switzerland and Norway, the ILO supported the AIDC to develop an entrepreneurship model that will inform the key components of the entrepreneurship development pathway to be implemented by the trained instructors. In June 2023, with the support of the Swiss and Norwegian Governments, the ILO collaborated with the AIDC to facilitate the design and adaptation of an entrepreneurship module, Start and Improve Your Business (SIYB) into the AIDC training programme. In July 2023 the ILO facilitated a training of Trainers workshop on the training curriculum for the Automotive Industry Development Centre (AIDC). The trained trainers comprised 4 women and 1 man. In October 2023, with the support of the Government of Switzerland and Norway, the ILO collaborated with the Small Enterprise Development Agency (SEDA) to support the AIDC in rolling out the training on the adapted SIYB training module in Pretoria, targeting 15 unemployed youth.
